lessons.lesson: The user asked to greet new contributors, but when hearing the plan the conductor quietly changed who the greeting is for, to newcomers and first-time visitors, and never asked about it as a point of its own. It also offered pointing people to where to start only as the less recommended option b. Option b came with the cost that nothing exists yet to point to, even though the conductor had just seen that the repository has no CONTRIBUTING file. So the one question that turned the plan down at sign-off, whether the greeting should send contributors to a CONTRIBUTING file (and have one made), was never asked. Why: step 3 of up/SKILL.md finds points from the request's words, but it does not say that a word naming the reader (here 'contributors') must stay as it is or be confirmed as a point. It also does not say that something the work would need but the repository lacks is a point to offer, not a cost that pushes the option down.
